cells.finding: The sqrt(3)-partner is NOT object-forced to be unique, and the admissible-partner family is large at two nested levels. Level 1 (field): the norm-+1 admission test is satisfied by the great majority of real quadratic fields (30/37=81% in a direct scan, and known-infinite by standard density results) — 'norm+1' is the generic condition, not a fine-tuned one. Level 2 (embedding, previously unflagged in this repo's record): even fixing the EXACT SAME field used in B1192's headline pair (disc 12, sqrt3), conjugating the partner matrix within its own GL2(Z)-class while holding the object A fixed changes the outcome — of 60 sampled relative embeddings, 22 reproduce the headline DIRECT(det=-1) result and 38 fall into a qualitatively different TORSOR regime (no integral realizer exists at all: the pair is GL2(Z)-inequivalent to its own mirror, not merely mirror-odd). The identical DIRECT(det=-1) outcome (single-signed, GL2(Z)-realized, restricting to c the same way M1's does) was independently exhibited and verified for THREE further, distinct discriminants under suitable embedding: disc 21 (17/36 samples), disc 15 (13/36), and disc 13 (23/120) — the last a genuine norm-(-1) field (fundamental unit 18+5*sqrt(13), norm -1, the same 'self-coupling-killed' type as A's own golden field), directly refuting norm+1 as a necessary condition for the heterogeneous DIRECT(-1) outcome once embedding freedom is admitted. Conversely, a wide 204-embedding scan of the norm-(-1) sqrt(2) control (GC-16's own dead control) reproduced ONLY DIRECT(+1) (mirror-even, dead) or TORSOR — never DIRECT(-1) — showing the achievable sign is a field-specific invariant that does not track the unit-norm dichotomy GC-2/GC-16 proposed. Net: 'which pair' is supplied at two levels (field and embedding), neither pinned down by the stated admission criterion, and the criterion itself (norm+1) is shown non-discriminating by a direct counterexample (disc 13). This is exactly the base-rate/generic-to-any-hyperbolic-pair failure mode this repo has hit before (B727/B993/B996); MB12 is satisfied because the search had a real chance of returning 'unique' (it did not fail to find alternatives) and did not.

  Step 3: confirm 𝔊/M are named and independently attested (K1) — an ad hoc "series that happens to work" without an identified algebra is REJECTED as numerology regardless of numeric fit.
  Step 4: confirm χ_∂ is derived from the object's own cover/cusp/holonomy/CS data (K6), not imported from an external CFT chosen for its central charge — cite the exact derivation.
  Step 5: run the Cardy/finite-N growth estimator (already coded in GC-6) on χ_∂ and confirm c_eff → 6 (K5), and state explicitly which cusp(s)/mechanism supply the missing 5 units beyond B262's one.
  A candidate passing all five steps CLOSES L154's remaining bridge and converts σ from an input to a derived quantity (deletes one row from the input floor). A candidate failing any step is logged with the step number and reason, exactly as B672 is logged here as a Step-0 failure.
